independent.summary: DELETE reads the passkey list first and only then runs the conditional `$pull`. Suppose a passwordless account has passkeys A and B, and two removals of A run at once. The first one wins and leaves only B. The second still finds A in the list it already loaded, its `$nor` condition fails because one passkey is left, and it gets `matchedCount === 0` and a 409 saying 'This passkey is the only way to sign in'. The right answer is a 404, because A is already gone.

grades.reason: accountReq throws a rejection carrying the status and message on any non-OK response, and PasskeySettings.load() catches it and shows loadError.
removePasskey goes through accountReq, which throws on any non-OK response, and remove() catches it and handles 401, 404 and 409 separately.
A test case that isn't there is not a defect, and add() already turns any registration failure into a generic error message.
Only one row can be confirming at a time, and while `busy` is set every Remove and Keep button is disabled, so a second removal can't start and the state can't get mixed up.

recordUse only changes the user document already in memory; if the passkey was removed in the meantime, the `__v` bump makes user.save() fail, and that failure is caught (500 at sign-in, a refusal message in passkeyRefusal).
requireAuth admits a request without `session.userId` only when it carries the bearer token, and turning that token away with a 403 is the intended session-only rule, not an access hole.
passkeyRefusal returns 'the passkey assertion did not verify' when `verification.verified` is false, so that path does return a value.
The test 'a sign-in records when it happened…' checks that `lastUsedAt` is at or after the time the sign-in started.
That same test clears deviceType and backedUp on a legacy passkey, then checks they come back as 'multiDevice' and true after a sign-in.

The DELETE test checks the 200 response body, that the stored passkeys are gone, that the removed passkey can no longer sign in, that a repeat removal is a 404, and that another account's passkey is a 404.
The passwordless test clears passwordHash, removes one of two passkeys, and checks that removing the last one is a 409 and it stays stored.

summary: All 11 local findings are false positives: they claim error handling or test checks are missing when the code and tests plainly have them, and the review missed the one real (minor) race in DELETE.
